title: Scoped Metric Projections: column-level RBAC and pipeline masking for console usage views
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The console exposes aggregated usage views and pre-aggregated metrics that currently rely on tenant-level gating only. Several customers have requested the ability to hide specific columns (e.g., user_id, session_token, raw_prompt) or derived metrics (per-user retention, developer_token_count) from lower-privilege roles. We need a solution that enforces column-level and derived-metric permissioning across both the query layer (console API) and the analytics pipelines that produce pre-aggregated tables.

Scope: Implement a policy-driven projection layer that: 1) lets admins create projection policies mapping roles to allowed metric/column sets, 2) enforces projection at API time for ad-hoc queries and saved views, and 3) applies masking or exclusion during ETL/pre-aggregation so downstream tables never store unauthorized columns for a given tenant/role. The solution must be performant, auditable, and compatible with existing role/tenant model in the console RBAC service.
acceptance_criteria: Projection policy CRUD in RBAC service (create/read/update/delete) with audit trail
Console API respects projection policy for ad-hoc queries and saved views; unauthorized columns are removed from responses
ETL jobs produce masked or reduced tables according to projection policy when job runs for a tenant with restrictive projections
Rollout behind feature flag with gradual ramp and metrics to validate correctness and performance
E2E tests and regression suite added to analytics CI verifying masking semantics for example tenants
Security review completed and signed off before GA
progress_updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting with Product, Analytics, and Security. Agreed on projection policy schema and audit requirements.
2025-01-20: Prototype projection enforcement added to console query sanitizer (branch: feat/column-projections). Initial micro-benchmarks show <5% tail latency increase for typical 3-column views.
2025-01-28: ETL pattern chosen: add projection-aware publisher that filters columns before writing to tenant-specific pre-agg tables; proof-of-concept working for daily_usage_summary pipeline.
2025-02-04: Design review with Security (notes in Confluence) — requested explicit logging for any masked field occurrences and a retention policy for masking audit logs.

2025-02-11: Integration tests added that validate both API masking and pre-agg masking; discovered edge-case around derived metrics that use excluded columns — added rule to auto-drop derived metrics when base columns are hidden.
2025-02-15: Preparing canary rollout plan and metrics dashboard; plan to enable for 5 internal tenants on 2025-02-20 behind feature flag.
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Patel): Prioritize clear admin UX for projection policy creation and preview before apply (requested mock in Figma)
Security (Daniel Morales): Require per-change approver and signed audit entry for any projection that reduces visibility of PII columns
Data Eng (Priya Shah): Suggested implementing a projection metadata table driving both API and ETL to avoid duplication of rules
SRE (Lena Gomez): Add slow-path instrumentation for queries that trigger on-the-fly masking to monitor tail latency and guide caching decisions
links: Incident reference: INC-2024-09-analytics-leak (lessons learned used to justify masking)
implementation_notes: We will represent projection policies as a small JSON policy stored in RBAC service with schema versioning (v1: allow/deny per-column and derived-metric). The console API will expand requested columns, intersect with allowed set, and either return a reduced projection or 403 if a saved view includes required-but-forbidden metric. ETL changes will be applied as a filter step in the publish stage: when a tenant has an active restrictive projection, the publisher writes a masked table (masked values replaced with NULL or aggregated buckets for counts) and sets a table metadata tag 'projection_applied=v1'. To avoid explosion of per-tenant tables, we will use partition-level masking for high-cardinality tenants and share masked tables where possible.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary for 5 tenants (feature flag on backend + UI hidden) -> monitor masking rate, query latency, and audit logs. Phase 2: opt-in beta for customers via support ticket + admin UI preview. Phase 3: GA with admin-approval workflow and retention of audit entries for 90 days. Metrics to watch: masked_field_rate, projection_cache_hit_rate, average_query_tail_99, and ETL job duration delta.
